intro: Searching for a building survey surveyor near you usually means you're buying a property and want a proper picture of its condition before you commit. A building survey is the most detailed inspection, so it's worth understanding what you'll get and who is best placed to carry it out locally. We can introduce you to a suitable UK surveyor near you, who will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a building survey surveyor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people behind this search are at a point in a purchase where they need a detailed condition report on a specific property, often one that is old, unusual or has been altered.
needs: You are buying an older or period home and want to know what defects and repairs the building survey reveals before you exchange.
You have had a mortgage valuation and realise it is not a condition report, so you want a fuller inspection of the property.
The property is large or has been extended and altered over the years, and you want a surveyor to explain how those changes have affected it.
You have spotted damp, movement or timber problems and want a surveyor to look at them properly rather than guess.
You want someone local who can visit the property and talk you through the findings in person.
context_heading: Understanding the building survey and who carries it out
context: A building survey is the most detailed inspection of a property's condition and is particularly suited to older, larger or altered homes. The report explains defects and the repairs they may need, which helps you decide how to proceed before exchange.

Many surveyors are members of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS), and RICS-regulated firms must follow professional standards, hold insurance and offer a complaints process. Chartered surveyors use the letters MRICS or FRICS, and you can check the RICS directory to confirm who you are dealing with.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the property, including its approximate age, type and whether it has been extended or altered.
Say what stage you are at, such as whether you have had an offer accepted or are close to exchange.
Mention any concerns you already have, such as damp, cracks or timber problems.
Confirm the property's location so we can introduce you to a surveyor near you.
Explain whether you need a full building survey or are unsure which report type suits the property.
Note whether the property is unusual in any way, such as a period home or a non-standard construction.
questions: Which type of report will I receive, and is it a building survey suited to this property?
Are you a member of RICS, and is your firm RICS-regulated?
Will you be independent of the sale and of any other party involved?
What will the report cover, and will it explain the defects and likely repairs?
How will you arrange access to the property, and what do you need from me?
Can you talk me through the findings once the report is ready?

faqs.q: Is a building survey the same as a mortgage valuation?
faqs.a: No. A mortgage valuation is carried out for the lender to confirm the property is worth lending against. A building survey is a much more detailed inspection of the property's condition, suited to older, larger or altered homes.

faqs.q: When should I book a building survey?
faqs.a: It is best booked before you exchange contracts, so you have the findings in time to act on them. That gives you the chance to discuss any defects and repairs with your surveyor before you are committed.

faqs.q: How do I check a surveyor's credentials?
faqs.a: Many surveyors are members of RICS, and chartered surveyors use the letters MRICS or FRICS. You can check the RICS directory and ask which report type you are getting and whether the surveyor is independent of the sale.

faqs.q: What if the property has damp or timber problems?
faqs.a: A building survey will report on defects it finds, including damp and timber issues. For specialist damp and timber work, the Property Care Association represents specialists in that field, so it is worth asking about relevant expertise.
